html:
SMTO-FIL-0051 — An edit to several files failed partway and needs checking

GUID: fb77455d-7419-40cf-a8ae-b708f917c498
Slug: file-patch-partial-failure
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • SMTO was changing several files together when something went wrong. It tried to put back the files it had already changed, but some may still hold the new text.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO which files in this edit were changed and which ones it put back. SMTO keeps a result for each file, so you learn which ones need a closer look.
  2. Ask SMTO to show the current contents of each of those files, or their differences, without changing them. Some files may already contain the change, so repeating the whole edit could apply it twice or fail again.
  3. Once you've checked, ask SMTO to apply only the changes that are still missing. Applying only what's missing avoids overwriting changes that already landed or that someone else made.

What success looks like

  • Every file in the edit shows the content you expect, and SMTO's next edit finishes without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run the same edit again until each file has been checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A multi-file patch failed during commit; per-file rollback ran, and its results (rollback, rollback_complete, partial_mutation) determine which files are restored, still changed or uncertain.

What this means

  • Multi-file patch commit raised an exception and entered per-file rollback handling, whose individual receipts may report restored or uncertain state. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Multi-file patch commit raised an exception and entered per-file rollback handling, whose individual receipts may report restored or uncertain state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect every commit and rollback receipt against current file contents; one rollback success does not prove all files restored.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the files and rollback arrays in the error result: entries with restored=false may hold the new content or outside edits. Compare each file's current revision with its before_revision and after_revision, reconcile the content, and only then apply a fresh patch against current revisions (expected_revisions); multi-file patches are not atomic.
  • Inspect every file commit and rollback receipt. Reconcile the actual contents before retrying any part of the patch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Each affected file has reconciled current content before further edits.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
